result:
I can't derive the classification independently here, and the proposed solution doesn't establish it either. The count of 13 comes from an informal tally over cases of Φ and gcd(Φ, B). No argument is given that each case yields exactly one regular family, that the cases are all realized by regular forms, or that the families are distinct. The bounds on deg Φ, deg B, deg C and deg D are also stated without justification. The solution itself gives no derivation that settles the number.

My recollection of the literature on Laguerre-Hahn forms of class zero is that the published count is smaller than 13, but I can't pin down the exact figure. That recollection, together with the unsupported counting, leads me to reject the answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
